feed.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT

entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
Standardizing transaction signing practices is critical for the robustness of blockchain protocols. Transactions should always be committed to the sequence of the same input, ensuring consistency and security in how inputs are referenced. The hashSequence commitment must only occur when every input and output within a transaction has been properly signed. This ensures the integrity of the entire transaction, preventing unauthorized modifications.
The upcoming iteration of SIGHASH will represent a significant evolution by introducing not just the NOINPUT mechanism, but also enabling the signing of additional components such as fees, previous scriptPubKey, and all input values. This development marks a departure from the relatively straightforward approach seen in BIP143, signaling the need for more comprehensive transaction validation methods.
Given these advancements, it may be more appropriate for BIP118 to transition into an informational BIP. Its primary focus should shift towards providing the rationale behind NOINPUT and illustrating its use through practical examples. Furthermore, cross-referencing with the consensus BIP would enhance understanding and foster alignment across related proposals, thereby strengthening the overall framework for transaction handling in Bitcoin and similar systems.
